case_summary: Follow-up staged demo investigation of a living room reported as flooded, documenting damaged belongings for recovery. Four files were reviewed (two room photos and two staged-demo receipts), within the 10-file combined cap. All eight belongings and all findings from the previous result keep their original IDs and meanings. The renter confirmed the brown leather Chesterfield armchair name and a purchase price of 650.00, confirmed that two red tubular-frame chairs were present, and clarified that the Northwind Home Goods receipt is for a lamp in the bedroom. Those confirmations close two findings and two questions, which are retained with status resolved rather than deleted, and a new finding records that the confirmed price has no document and no currency. No receipt is matched to any visible object, no brand, model, purchase date, currency or loss date is verifiable from the evidence, and no damage, cause, ownership, payout or coverage conclusion is drawn.

evidence.description: Wide, split-level view of a living room with a horizontal waterline across the lower third. Above the line: pale patterned wallpaper, two framed prints on the left wall, a dark two-shade pendant fixture, a cluster of four hanging globe bulbs over the windows, red tubular-frame seating and a low table near a bright multi-pane window, and a large brown armchair at the right. A wicker chair back is clipped at the far left edge. The below-waterline area is an even, mirror-like blue rendering containing strongly recoloured shapes (keyboard, guitar, cushion, typewriter, buckets); it reads as a manipulated composite rather than a documentary underwater photograph.

Closer view of the same brown armchair at the waterline, in front of the two right-hand windows. Shows rolled arms, a broad column of button tufting, mottled reddish-brown upholstery and a jagged, stained waterline across the seat and skirt. Brownish debris lies on the water surface at both lower corners, and a small vase of dried stems is partly visible at the lower left. Per the supplied manifest this image is a crop of ev_001 and not an independent camera position.

Single-page synthetic receipt from 'NORTHWIND HOME GOODS (fictional store, demo only)' headed '** STAGED DEMO - NOT A REAL RECEIPT **'. Prints 'Date: 03/04/2024' and 'Order #: DEMO-20817', one line for a floor lamp, brass finish with a white linen drum shade, 62 in, 'Item # NW-LMP-4410' at 89.99, then Subtotal 89.99, Tax 8.10, TOTAL 98.09, and 'Paid: card ending 0000 (demo)'. No lamp answering this description is visible in either photo, and the renter states the lamp was in the bedroom.

Single-page synthetic grocery receipt from 'GREENLEAF MARKET (fictional store, demo only)' headed '** STAGED DEMO - NOT A REAL RECEIPT **'. Prints 'Date: Jan 12 2025' and four lines: Bananas 2 lb 1.38, Whole milk 1 gal 4.29, Sourdough bread 5.49, Eggs dozen 3.99, TOTAL 15.15. No order number, item number or SKU is printed. Contains no furniture or household goods.

findings.explanation: Both photos show one brown tufted armchair with the same rolled-arm profile, the same mottled upholstery and the same stained horizontal tide line, in front of the same pair of right-hand windows. ev_002 is, per the manifest, a tighter crop of ev_001, and a crop counts as a same-object pair exactly like a second angle: the finding is raised so the chair is counted once, enumerated from the canonical view ev_001, and recorded singly as itm_001.

A small vase of dried stems appears at the bottom-left of ev_002 and at the lower-left of ev_001 beside the armchair. Both files show the same small vase, and because ev_002 is a crop of ev_001 the pair would otherwise be counted twice; recorded once as itm_008, enumerated from ev_001.

The ev_003 receipt prints one line for a brass-finish floor lamp with a white linen drum shade, 62 in, 'Item # NW-LMP-4410', for 89.99. No floor lamp answering that description is visible in either photo, and the renter has now stated that no brass floor lamp was in this room and that the Northwind receipt is for a lamp in the bedroom. The line therefore stays unmatched and no receipt match is proposed for any item in this room.
findings.resolution_reason: Renter confirmed no brass floor lamp was in this room and that the Northwind receipt is for a lamp in the bedroom.

findings.explanation: The ev_004 receipt lists groceries only (Bananas 2 lb 1.38, Whole milk 1 gal 4.29, Sourdough bread 5.49, Eggs dozen 3.99, TOTAL 15.15). No visible object in either photo corresponds to any line, so every line is left unmatched. It is not in conflict with ev_003, which is a different vendor, date and category.

Neither photo shows a label, brand mark, model number, serial tag, maker's stamp or date. Brand, model and purchase date are therefore null for every item, and ownership is unverified for all of them because the room may have been furnished by a landlord or a previous tenant.

ev_001 is a split-level composite with an even blue underwater band containing recoloured, mirrored shapes (keyboard, guitar, cushion, typewriter, buckets). That below-waterline portion is not treated as a documentary record, so no object is enumerated from it and no condition observation is made there. No damage, cause or ownership conclusion is drawn from either photo.

There is no independent second viewpoint of the room. Because ev_002 is derived from ev_001, hidden areas (chair underside and legs, table base, the wall behind the armchair, the right-hand wall, the rest of the room off-frame) are documented nowhere. Any item whose base or full extent matters needs a separate, uncropped photo.

The red tubular seating could not be resolved into a definite count from the photo: one ladder-profile frame is clearly visible while a second red seat shape appears immediately to its right near the window, which may be a second chair or a waterline reflection. The renter has since confirmed that there were two red tubular-frame chairs. That confirmed wording is recorded verbatim in itm_006 and the ambiguity is closed here rather than being deleted.
findings.resolution_reason: Renter confirmed the count is two red tubular-frame chairs.

findings.explanation: The confirmed name and a purchase price of 650.00 for itm_001 are preserved verbatim, but no document backs that figure: neither receipt is for an armchair, no currency is supplied or printed anywhere in the evidence, and no purchase date is stated. Currency and purchase_date therefore remain null rather than being inferred from the receipt style or locale.

questions.reason: The ev_003 receipt prints exactly that lamp at 89.99, but no lamp of that description is visible in ev_001 or ev_002, so the line stays unmatched.
questions.resolution_reason: Renter confirmed no brass floor lamp was in this room; the Northwind receipt is for a lamp in the bedroom.

questions.reason: One ladder-profile frame is clear, plus a second red seat shape that may be a second chair or a waterline reflection.

questions.reason: Both look like fixed or hardwired fixtures with no receipt, so it is unclear whether they are personal belongings or the landlord's fittings.

questions.reason: The wide view is a composite with a stylised underwater band and the close-up is a crop of it, so the room has only one true viewpoint.

questions.reason: The confirmed price is preserved exactly as '650.00', but no currency was supplied and none is printed on any evidence file, so the currency field stays null.

questions.question: Should the bedroom lamp on the Northwind Home Goods receipt be documented in a separate bedroom investigation, and can you send a photo of that lamp?
questions.reason: The renter confirmed the lamp belongs to the bedroom, so it is outside this living-room record and is currently documented only as an unmatched receipt.

limitations: Staged demo case: both receipts are fictional, are headed 'STAGED DEMO - NOT A REAL RECEIPT', and are treated only as demo material rather than proof of purchase; two unrelated receipts are not reported as conflicting with each other.

Follow-up run: every item_id, finding_id and question_id from the previous result is preserved unchanged and no ID was reassigned; resolved findings and questions stay in place with a one-line resolution_reason instead of being deleted.
The attached photos are stock/composite imagery rather than the renter's own documentary photographs; ev_001 is a split-level composite with a mirrored, recoloured underwater band.

The supplied manifest states that ev_002 is cropped from ev_001. The crop is treated as a same-object pair and still produces possible_duplicate findings fnd_001 and fnd_002, so neither the armchair nor the vase is counted twice.

Manifest filenames are recorded verbatim, but each omits the platform's upload hash suffix; every manifest entry was bound to the single attachment sharing that base name, and no entry was re-pointed to a different file.

The renter confirmed a purchase price of 650.00 for itm_001 without stating a currency and without supplying a receipt, so purchase_price is recorded as the confirmed string and currency remains null (finding fnd_009, question q_006).
itm_006 keeps review_status needs_review because only the count of two chairs was confirmed; ownership, brand, model, purchase date and price are still unverified for that item.
No brand, model, serial number, purchase date, currency or loss date is visible or supplied beyond the renter-confirmed armchair name and price; all such values are null rather than estimated.
No replacement cost, payout, coverage, liability or insurer-approval assessment is made, and no damage, cause or ownership conclusion is drawn from the photos.
Only 8 visible belongings could be distinguished; objects under the waterline, off-frame, or indeterminate in the composite were deliberately not enumerated.
